US economic momentum is accelerating:

The S&P Global US Composite PMI index surged +1.5 points in August, to 56.0, the highest since April 2022.

This marks the 3rd consecutive monthly improvement.

This comes as the Services PMI index jumped +2.2 points, to 56.8, the highest since March 2022.

At the same time, the Manufacturing PMI index fell -0.7 points, to 53.9, the lowest in 5 months but still firmly in expansion territory.

Meanwhile, businesses added workers at the strongest pace since January 2025, led by hiring in the services sector.

This data implies a +3.0% annualized YoY GDP growth for Q3 2026, up from +1.5% in Q2.

AI is driving a historic wave of growth.

South Korea's chip boom is incredible. 

South Korea's chip trade surplus surged to a record ~$35 billion in June, more than tripling in 12 months.

By comparison, the non-chip trade surplus was just ~$1 billion over the same period.

Meanwhile, semiconductor exports soared +198.8% YoY in the first 20 days of August, and shipments of computer-related products jumped +242.1% YoY.

As a result, South Korea’s overall exports surged +61.5% YoY over this period, marking the 2nd consecutive month of growth above +60.0%, following July’s +62.9%.

AI has transformed South Korea’s chip sector into a global industry.

Investors are rotating from semiconductors and software into the broader tech sector.

tweets.text:
$146 billion of software loans sit exactly where AI does the most damage.

Application software carries that whole load, and most of it is rated B- or lower. The parts AI helps, cybersecurity and infrastructure, carry a fraction: about $28B and $21B.

These firms charge by the seat for work AI can automate. The revenue that services the debt is the revenue AI eats. If seat counts fall, B- slides to CCC, and the default risk lands on the private-credit funds holding the paper.
